checks: A 25 MiB file uses the default executable wrapper, arrives by email without attachments, and downloads with a private seven-day signature.
Two files with identical names and contents receive distinct links and Spanish expiry lines.
Source mutation during upload cannot change scanned bytes, hashes, sizes, or earlier linked content; private snapshots are removed.
A later same-day send of changed content leaves earlier links unchanged.
A file exactly at the attachment cap remains an attachment with unchanged bytes.
Home settings support a relative override and custom note, while environment settings take priority.
An oversized dry run shows planned link delivery and expiry without uploading, emailing, or logging.
Missing confirmation, the total size cap, a missing wrapper, and secret scanning all prevent uploads and mail.
A real rclone signing failure returns exit 7, records the error, and sends no email.
An unusable override falls back to the executable default wrapper.
An SMTP connection failure returns exit 7 and records a masked error without signed URLs.
An unavailable upload endpoint returns exit 7, sends no email, and removes the private snapshot.
The private audit log records attachment/link mode and per-file expiry without URLs, file contents, or passwords.
